prompt: Create an ambitious original editorial COLLAGE artwork for the full-bleed opening of a computing-history magazine website. Very wide horizontal panorama, ideally 3:1. This is finished visual art, NOT a webpage mockup, NOT a diagram, no headings or labels, no arrows or node connections, no readable text. An evocative physical cut-paper/photographic-halftone assemblage suggesting that computing connects people, institutions, engineering, programming, games, music, and cultures across the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Strong agency-quality art direction, decisive asymmetry and overlaps. Bone-paper ground #f6f4ee with carbon black, oxidised copper/vermillion and small blue-green accents; crisp collage silhouettes, convincing photocopy and screenprint textures, occasional vivid pixel colour. Across the OUTER EDGES arrange fragments: at left anonymous mid-century human figures (a woman and a man, equal visual weight, neither identifiable as a real person, non-photoreal expressive halftone printed silhouettes), a closeup human hand, punched paper tape curling out of a stack of anonymous machine-printed paper, a sliver of brass calculating mechanism; at right fragments of integrated circuit packages and PCB traces, a partial reel-to-reel spool and vinyl groove suggesting music, a generic keyboard fragment with no logos or legible key labels, a small raster-pixel burst and CRT phosphor pattern. Some paper layers travel diagonally across the frame, other elements break out of the panorama's edges. The forms overlap and echo each other so relationships are felt, never explained. Human elements are part of a balanced larger mix, not the organising theme. No one machine dominates. Reserve a large genuinely QUIET paper-coloured area across the central 35 percent of the panorama for a separate live website title, with only very faint edge intrusions there; keep important dark objects and faces outside that central title area. It must feel tactile, daring and editorial, not a sepia nostalgia scrapbook, not a stock technology montage, not a cyberpunk poster. No stars, no galaxies, no literal network lines, no cards, boxes, caption panels, flags, military insignia, company logos, fake historic photographs, named persons, counterfeit archival documents or fake readable code. All scene elements are deliberately stylised original illustration, not documentary evidence. Full bleed to every outer edge, no border, no frame, no text.
rights: Original generated artwork; no third-party photograph, portrait, scan, logo or software capture supplied. Illustrative figures and artefacts are imagined, not named historical subjects or archival evidence.
processing: Proportional resize and WebP encoding only. The responsive layout arranges the illustration and live title as separate layers; the landscape may crop at intermediate viewport ratios.
